title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries depleted while the cars were stuck in severe traffic. Multiple Jaguar I-PACE models required towing after gridlock near the Golden Gate Bridge following a fireworks display. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported.

The deployment assumed the vehicles could operate safely through major traffic disruptions and unplanned road closures. The system lacked sufficient battery capacity or routing logic to avoid becoming trapped during foreseeable high-traffic events in a dense urban area. Catching this would have required either testing the vehicles' behavior under the traffic conditions that actually occurred on July Fourth, or restricting their operation during known high-congestion periods.

It is not established whether the company had advance warning of the specific traffic patterns that developed, or what battery reserve policies were in place before the incident.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries depleted while stuck in severe traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up after a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported. A passenger named Rose Peterson described the car continuing to drive during the chaotic scene.

Following the incident, Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie warned residents about post-fireworks congestion and urged patience while streets cleared. The city's Department of Emergency Management had previously warned of heavy traffic and crowded transit. Lutvak, the mayor's press secretary, announced that city officials will hold conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother traffic management for future events, acknowledging that over 100,000 people in the area experienced delays.
